---
title: Architecture
guide-section: Development
---

## Layout

| path | holds |
|---|---|
| `src/ha_automations/apps/` | AppDaemon apps and their settings models |
| `src/ha_automations/fades.py`, `curves.py` | fade logic and math, no Home Assistant imports |
| `src/ha_automations/detectors/` | light level sources |
| `src/ha_automations/triggers.py` | triggers that start fades |
| `src/ha_automations/lights.py` | lights that fades write to |
| `src/ha_automations/config.py` | `Config`, the base settings model |
| `deploy/appdaemon/apps/` | one-line shims that AppDaemon loads, importing the app class from the package |
| `scripts/deploy.sh` | deploys a tag to Home Assistant OS |
| `docs/`, `index.qmd`, `great-docs.yml` | this site |

Logic goes in `src/ha_automations/`. The shims hold nothing else. `apps.yaml` lives in a private config repo.

## How an app starts

1. AppDaemon reads `apps.yaml`, imports the shim named by `module`, and calls `initialize()` on `class`.
2. `LightFadeApp.initialize` drops the keys AppDaemon itself uses (`APPDAEMON_KEYS`) and validates the rest with the app's `Settings` model. Unknown keys are an error (`Config` sets `extra="forbid"`).
3. It builds a `LightFade` from the settings, the detector and a `HassLight`.
4. It registers each `start` trigger and the test event to call `start()`, and the detector to call `update()`.

## Settings are the docs

Each settings field has a `Field(description=...)`. The app pages render the settings tables, defaults and charts from the models at build time, so the docs follow the code. A test fails if a field has no description.
